post.summary: Record a route (idempotent)
post.description:
Stores a route the field app recorded: the ordered rooms a technician walked, and the ordered assets they worked inside each room. The route belongs to the SITE (`sld_id`), so every later work order on that site lists and can follow it; `recorded_in_session_id` only records which work order the walk happened during.

`id` is CLIENT-GENERATED and authoritative — the device saved the route locally and is already referencing it. Replaying a create with an id that already exists returns **200 with the stored row untouched** (the offline queue retries), never 409 and never a duplicate.

`stops[]` (with their `assets[]`) are written as one atomic set; there are no stop- or asset-level endpoints. `stop_count` is recomputed server-side and a client value is ignored. `created_at` / `visited_at` are stored exactly as sent, because the device may have been offline for days. `created_by_name` and `recorded_in_session_name` are read-side joins the server returns and clients never send.

Requires `routes.manage` AND an assignment to the work order named by `recorded_in_session_id`; a payload that omits that field skips the assignment check, since there is no work order to be assigned to.

Raised for a room or asset that does not belong to the route's site, stop positions that are not exactly 0..n-1, asset positions inside a stop that are not unique and ascending, a work order on a different site than the route, a stop position that does not exist on the route, a current_position outside 0..stop_count, or a user id (`created_by`, `user_id`, `stops[].completed_by`, `assets[].processed_by`) that belongs to another organization.

The body carries the offending field BOTH ways: `field` / `message` as the feature spec asks, and an `errors[]` array as the rest of this API's validation responses do.

put.summary: Rename, delete, or re-stop a route
put.description:
One endpoint for three edits, and a caller sends only what changed:

* `name` — rename.
* `is_deleted: true` — SOFT delete. A route is never hard-deleted; runs referencing it stay as history, and devices that pull the tombstone drop the route and abandon their runs on it.
* `stops[]` — FULL REPLACEMENT of the stop set (this is how a route edited in place during a follow is saved). Omitting `stops` leaves the existing stops alone, which is NOT the same as sending `[]`.

**`stops: null` is NOT the same as `stops: []`.** An omitted or null `stops` leaves the existing stops untouched; only a real list replaces them. (Serializers that emit explicit nulls for nullable fields are safe to point at this endpoint.)

Requires `routes.manage` AND an assignment to **some** work order on the route's site — not necessarily the one it was recorded during, since editing an inherited route from another work order is the normal flow. There is no creator or admin check beyond that (Q4-B). `modified_at` is set by the SERVER; the request that arrives last wins.

post.summary: Start following a route (idempotent, 409 to adopt)
post.description:
Creates the WORK ORDER's progress through one route. Progress is scoped to the work order, not the user: one work order is assigned to one technician, so progress belongs to the job and survives a device swap or a reassignment. `user_id` records who STARTED the run and never scopes reads.

**A work order has at most one ACTIVE run.** If a DIFFERENT run is already ACTIVE for this `session_id`, the response is **409 whose body is that run's RouteRunDto** — first-to-sync wins, and the losing device parses the body to ADOPT the server's run and mark its own local one abandoned. `success: false` and `error: "active_run_exists"` ride alongside the DTO fields.

Replaying a create with a known `id` returns 200 with the stored run. `stops[]` are COMPLETION rows (one per completed stop, `completed_by: null` meaning it completed automatically once every stop asset was worked); `assets[]` are manual "processed" marks. `current_position` is stored and echoed but is INFORMATIONAL — the current stop is derived client-side as the first live stop with no completion row.

Requires `routes.manage` and an assignment to the work order.

A tombstoned route cannot be followed — drop it locally and abandon runs on it rather than retrying the create. (`PUT /route_run/update/{run_id}` stays open on a deleted route, so the resulting ABANDONED status can still be synced.)

put.summary: Record visit completions, finish, pause or resume a run
put.description:
The single write the field app coalesces a whole offline walk into.

`stops[]` and `assets[]` are FULL REPLACEMENT and may **shrink** — unmarking a visit removes a completion row, so this is never append-only. Every status transition is legal, including the two reopening ones: `FINISHED -> ACTIVE` (unmarking a visit reopens a finished run) and `ABANDONED -> ACTIVE` (ABANDONED means PAUSED; following the route again resumes that same run with its completion rows and `started_at` intact).

Reactivating a run answers **409 with the work order's existing ACTIVE run** if it already has a different one, exactly like the create. `modified_at` is server-set; last write to arrive wins.

Requires `routes.manage` and an assignment to the work order the run belongs to — not merely being the run's `user_id`.

    This is the issue form's inline "add to library" action: the user has just
    written a title / description / resolution on a real issue and wants the
    next person to be offered the same wording. Everything about WHICH set
    receives it is resolved server-side — see `_writable_set_for_class` — so
    the client only says what the wording is and which asset class it is for.

    Gated on `issues.manage`, not `company_data.manage`: this is authored from
    the issue screen by the crew who write issues, and requiring the Builder's
    grant would put the button in front of exactly the people who cannot press
    it. The Builder surface keeps its stricter gate for wholesale set editing.

post.summary: Write the accepted fills onto the work order's form instances.
post.description:
Write the accepted fills onto the work order's form instances.

    Body: {"accept": [{"instance_id": "...", "submit": true,
                       "reject_decisions": ["d4", ...],
                       "added_values": {"<dotted path>": "<value>"}}, ...]}

    `added_values` are what the reviewer typed in — answers to the model's
    open questions, or fields the page never recorded. They go through the
    SAME validation as the model's own values (real path, legal option, right
    type, not already answered): a value a person typed is not a value the
    platform can store wrongly.

    A rejected decision takes its values with it — that is the point of
    making the reviewer's unit the CALL rather than the field. Rejecting the
    `match` decision rejects the whole fill: if this record is not this
    asset, nothing under it belongs here.

    Omit `accept` to take every fill the pipeline marked auto_submit — what
    the "apply the clean ones" button sends.

post.summary: Undo an apply: back to draft, and remove the values this job wrote.
post.description:
Undo an apply: back to draft, and remove the values this job wrote.

    The point of auto-submitting the clean ones is that nobody has to check
    them; the price of that is one button that takes a bad batch back. A
    value is only removed if it still equals what we wrote — anything a
    person has since edited is theirs and stays.

post.summary: Services available to a set of assets
post.description:
The batch twin of `GET /api/implementation-methods/available-for-node/{node_id}`: which services apply to ANY of the given assets, and how many of them each one covers. Same match as the single-asset route — by the asset's node-class KEY, non-corrective services the caller's company can use (plus globals, a global hidden by a live company fork), only services with an implementation method for that class. Two queries plus one batched site-access check — a fixed number whatever the batch size.

Body: `{node_ids: [uuid]}`, 1 to 5000. Assets that are unknown, deleted, or on a site the caller cannot reach are left out and returned in `ignored_node_ids` rather than failing the batch. `services` is ordered by `node_count` (most first), then name. Auth only — no permission gate, same as available-for-node.

200.description: Services covering at least one of the assets

400.description: node_ids missing, malformed, or more than 5000

    Runs the real evaluator (resolve_scope_assets with an include scope), so

get.summary: Service procedure rules, for offline evaluation
get.description:
The read-only sibling of `GET /api/implementation-methods/evaluate-for-node/{node_id}`: instead of answering "which methods apply to THIS asset" online, it ships the rules themselves so the app can answer it on-device with no connection and reach the same result.

Returns every non-corrective service the caller's company can use (the `GET /api/procedures-v2/services` set), each with its procedures keyed by node-class key, the procedure's ordered rules, and the implementation methods those rules name, with each method's form ids. Auth only — no permission gate, so a custom role without `procedures.view` can still sync. Optional `service_id` narrows it to one service.

Evaluating a rule set: find the procedure whose `node_class_key` is the asset's class, walk `rules` IN ORDER, and take the first rule whose `when` matches. That rule's `methods` is the answer — an empty list means the asset is OUT OF SCOPE, never a fall-through to the next rule. A rule with `when: {}` matches everything.

Conditions: `node_subtype` and `com` are list membership; `mains_type` matches the enum label (MCB / MLO / FDS / NFDS / Fuse / Non); `pole_count` and `system_voltage` take an operator object (`gt` / `gte` / `lt` / `lte` / `eq`). `system_voltage` is the DERIVED system voltage — the value the server walks up the SLD from the voltage authorities, the same number the node endpoints serialize — not the asset's own stored voltage field, which most assets do not carry. A condition whose asset value is null matches NOTHING. `node_subtype` arrives as stable KEYS, never ids, and an EMPTY list matches nothing (it means no id in the stored rule resolves to a key) — do not read it as a wildcard. `com` is compared without type coercion. Any other condition key, `issue_class` and `issue_subcategory` included, matches nothing outside a corrective context, which this bundle never covers.

**Record sections (task #124):** a method whose forms feed a typed record carries `record_sinks` — `"fsa"` (fluid samples) and / or `"torque"` (torque records); the key is absent on every other method. An asset shows Fluid Samples / Torque Records when it already has records of that kind, or when the methods a service evaluates to it include one that feeds it. Infrared and Ultrasonic follow the same rule keyed on the service's type (`IR` / `IR Checklist`, `UT`). A `TV` / `DGA` service (task #109) feeds its record by type — the torque log / fluid sample is entered natively, no form carries it — so each of its methods lists `"torque"` / `"fsa"` too. `GET /api/node/{node_id}/record-sections` is the server's answer to the same question.

200.description: Rules for every service this company can use

The GHOST SOURCE for a new instance: the most recent SUBMITTED instance

    The client renders these values as blue placeholder text in the empty
    fields of the new instance and materializes the untouched ones into the
    real submission on Submit — see ``egFormRendererShared.js``
    (``resolveGhostSource`` / ``materializeGhosts``) and iOS
    ``EGFormGhosts.swift``.

    SELECTION RULE — mirrored on iOS, which resolves the same row LOCALLY from
    SwiftData so preloading works offline (the SLD sync bundle already ships
    every instance linked to any of the SLD's nodes). Keep the two in lockstep:

        same eg_form_id, linked to this node (mapping not deleted),
        not deleted, submitted == True, id != ``exclude``,
        form_submission non-empty      →  newest by created_at

    TENANT SCOPING: gated on the NODE, not the instance —
    ``sld_scoped_first(Node, node_id)`` (node -> sld -> company). The
    pin/unpin helper ``_eg_form_instance_owning_company_id`` can't be used
    here: it resolves through ``instance.session_id`` and fails closed for
    task-driven instances, which are exactly the ones that carry a prior
    year's submitted record. A foreign/unknown node reads as 404 either way,
    so there is no existence leak.

    breaker's default trip unit is auto-assigned. They sometimes need
    to swap to a different trip unit (retrofitted, replaced, or
    intentionally over-spec'd). This endpoint powers the
    "Change Trip Unit" picker.

    Query params:
        current_style_id  int (optional) — used to derive the
                          (manufacturer, type) anchor for the priority
                          grouping. Without it everything is
                          group_priority=2.
        sensor_amps       int (optional) — restrict to trip units that
                          carry a sensor with this exact rating.
        plug_amps         int (optional) — when paired with sensor_amps,
                          further restrict to trip units whose matching
                          sensor exposes a plug at this exact rating.
        search            str (optional) — free-text matched against
                          manufacturer / type / style.
        limit             int (default 500, capped at 5000) — total
                          rows returned across all groups.

    Returns:
        [
          { style_id, manufacturer, type, style, group_priority },
          …
        ]
    where group_priority is:
        0 = same (manufacturer, type) as current — "Variants"
        1 = same manufacturer, different type — "Families"
        2 = different manufacturer — "Anything goes"
    Rows are ordered (priority asc, manufacturer, type, style).

        "success": true,

        "curve": [{"amps": 504, "time": 96.0}, ...],
        "band": [{"amps": 504, "tMin": 76.8, "tMax": 115.2}, ...],
        "method": 0,

get.summary: Get all active legal document versions (public).
Get the full CloudFront URL for the active legal document.
Check current user's pending legal document acceptances.
get.description:
Check current user's pending legal document acceptances.

    ZP-3784: `has_prior_acceptance` says whether this user has ever accepted any
    legal document. The client chooses its presentation from that — a full-page
    gate for someone who never has, an in-app prompt for someone mid-session.
    It cannot be derived from the pending set: a long-standing user shown a
    brand-new Privacy Policy has one pending document with no prior version, and
    would otherwise be treated as a first-time acceptor.

    Each pending document also carries previously_accepted_version — the last
    version of THAT document the user accepted, or null — which is what
    distinguishes an amended document from one they are seeing for the first
    time, for copy like "what changed".

    Auth: Bearer token (required)
    Headers: X-Subdomain (required)

    Response 200:
    {
        "all_accepted": false,
        "has_prior_acceptance": true,
        "pending": {
            "terms_and_conditions": {
                "id": "uuid",
                "document_type": "terms_and_conditions",
                "version": "2.0",
                "title": "Terms & Conditions",
                "content_url": "https://{subdomain}.egalvanic.ai/legal/terms-and-conditions/v2.0/document.pdf",
                "content_hash": "sha256...",
                "pdf_content_url": "https://{subdomain}.egalvanic.ai/legal/terms-and-conditions/v2.0/document.pdf | null",
                "pdf_content_hash": "sha256... | null",
                "summary_of_changes": "Updated liability clause",
                "effective_date": "2026-03-17T00:00:00Z",
                "is_active": true,
                "published_by": "uuid | null",
                "created_at": "2026-03-17T00:00:00Z",
                "previously_accepted_version": "2.0 | null"
            },
            "privacy_policy": { ... }
        }
    }

    Response 400: { "error": "X-Subdomain header is required" }

get.summary: Serve a legal document version's published bytes.
get.description:
Serve a legal document version's published bytes.

    ZP-3784: this is the RENDER artifact — what the acceptance gate displays (a
    PDF through the in-app viewer, HTML in a sandboxed iframe so its own
    stylesheet applies). What the user keeps is served by
    GET /legal/documents/<id>/download, which prefers the PDF published alongside
    an HTML document.

    Served here rather than from the public CloudFront path so the render behaves
    the same locally as when deployed, and so the document stays behind auth.

    Auth: Bearer token (required)

    Response 200: the stored document, Content-Type application/pdf (or text/html
                  for a version published before this change), inline, with the
                  content hash as an ETag.
    Response 304: If-None-Match matched — a version's bytes never change.
    Response 404: { "error": "Legal document version not found" }

get.summary: Download a legal document version.
get.description:
Download a legal document version.

    ZP-3784: serves the PDF published for keeping when there is one, and otherwise
    the render artifact itself — so the download always produces the document. A
    version published as a PDF is returned byte for byte, with no second copy
    stored for the two to drift apart.

    Auth: Bearer token (required)

    Response 200: attachment; application/pdf, or text/html for a version
                  published as HTML with no PDF alongside it
    Response 304: If-None-Match matched
    Response 404: { "error": "Legal document version not found" }

post.summary: Record user's acceptance of a legal document version.
post.description:
Record user's acceptance of a legal document version.

    Auth: Bearer token (required)

        "accepted_via": "web | mobile_ios | mobile_android",  (optional, default "web")
        "acceptance_method": "explicit_click | modal_prompt", (optional, default "explicit_click")

        "accepted_at": "2026-03-17T12:00:00Z",

post.summary: Upload a document and publish it as a new legal document version.
post.description:
Upload a document and publish it as a new legal document version.
    Deactivates the previous active version. The file is uploaded to S3
    and content_hash (SHA-256) is computed automatically.

    ZP-3784: `file` is what the gate renders; `pdf_file` is the optional PDF the
    user downloads. Publishing HTML for rendering and a PDF for keeping is the
    normal case — the HTML reflows and carries its own stylesheet, the PDF is the
    artifact worth keeping. A PDF `file` needs no `pdf_file`: it serves both, and
    storing the same bytes twice would only let the copies drift. The render
    format is detected from the bytes and kept as the S3 object's content type.

    Auth: Bearer token + users.manage permission
    Content-Type: multipart/form-data

    Form fields:
        file:                the RENDER artifact — HTML or PDF         (required)
        pdf_file:            the DOWNLOAD artifact, a PDF             (optional)
        document_type:       "terms_and_conditions" | "privacy_policy" (required)
        version:             "1.0"                                     (required)
        title:               "Terms & Conditions"                      (required)
        effective_date:      "2026-03-17T00:00:00Z"                   (optional, defaults to now)
        summary_of_changes:  "Initial version"                        (optional)

    Response 201:
    {
        "id": "uuid",
        "document_type": "terms_and_conditions",
        "version": "1.0",
        "title": "Terms & Conditions",
        "content_url": "terms-and-conditions/v1.0/document.pdf",
        "content_hash": "sha256 (auto-computed)",
        "pdf_content_url": "terms-and-conditions/v1.0/document.pdf | null",
        "pdf_content_hash": "sha256 (auto-computed) | null",
        "summary_of_changes": "Initial version",
        "effective_date": "2026-03-17T00:00:00Z",
        "is_active": true,
        "published_by": "uuid",
        "created_at": "2026-03-17T00:00:00Z"
    }

    Response 400: { "error": "document_type, version, and title are required" }
    Response 400: { "error": "file is required" }
    Response 400: { "error": "file was sent as a PDF but is not a PDF document" }
    Response 400: { "error": "document_type must be terms_and_conditions or privacy_policy" }

    it goes on the printed change-order document. Staging does NOT touch the

post.description:
Dry-render {"instructions_after": {...}} against an accepted plan and

    the delta back to the user BEFORE staging.

get.summary: Per-asset DERIVED features for the plan's site — the exact snapshot the
get.description:
Per-asset DERIVED features for the plan's site — the exact snapshot the
    engine matches selectors against: power scheme (BFS over the SLD) and
    derived voltage, plus class/subtype/COM/location/attributes. `com` is the
    PM view (NULL → 1 with com_defaulted; 4 → null with non_serviceable);
    `serviceability` is the selector vocabulary, DERIVED from com.
    Use this to answer "which assets are generator-fed?" / "what's under 480V?"
    and to sanity-check selectors before writing them.

    NOTE: voltage is currently resolved from the node's (or parent's) voltage
    enum — the full BFS voltage flood port is pending; assets with null voltage
    won't match voltage selectors.

put.summary: Apply schedule-line deviations, then re-generate the plan.
put.description:
Apply schedule-line deviations, then re-generate the plan.

    Body:
      {
        "deviations": [
          {"note": "why", "match": {"workorder_ids"?: [...], "service_ids"?: [...],
                                    "node_ids"?: [...], "node_class_keys"?: [...],
                                    "com"?: [3]},
           "action": {"set_methods"?: [mid], "add_methods"?: [mid],
                      "remove_methods"?: [mid], "est_mins"?: 45, "exclude"?: true}}
        ],
        "mode": "append"   # or "replace" — replace discards existing deviations
      }

    match dims AND'd (values within a dim OR'd); action applied to every
    matching schedule line; hours/labor/forms/pricing recompute downstream.
    Returns the new program totals + per-workorder est so the agent can report
    the effect of its edit.

post.summary: Create a v2 QUOTE from selected issues — the sibling of
post.description:
Create a v2 QUOTE from selected issues — the sibling of
    ``/ir_session/<id>/add-issues`` (Add to Work Order) on the sales side.

    The corrective service is evaluated exactly as it would be for a work
    order, but scoped to ONLY the assets carrying the selected issues: the
    quote's instructions declare one ad-hoc work item (service × those
    node_ids), and the engine's corrective path resolves each asset's open
    issues against the service's rules.

    Body: {issue_ids: [uuid], title, opportunity_id?, service_id?, sld_id?,
           date?}. title is required; without opportunity_id the quote gets
    its own hidden opportunity (task #140). service_id is normally
    omitted: the corrective service is resolved server-side, not user-picked.
    Returns the created + rendered plan.

post.summary: Add issues to an EXISTING issues-sourced quote — the "existing quote"
post.description:
Add issues to an EXISTING issues-sourced quote — the "existing quote"
    arm of the Add to Quote dialog. Body: {issue_ids: [uuid]}.

    Same gates as /plans/from-issues: tenant-scoped issues, every one with
    an ACCEPTED resolution, single site — and here the site must be the
    plan's. The corrective work item's scopes (issue_ids + node_ids) and the
    plan's provenance union in the new issues, then the plan re-renders;
    pricing edits live in instructions.pricing and survive untouched.

post.summary: Export a site walk to a v2 QUOTE (standard plan).
post.description:
Export a site walk to a v2 QUOTE (standard plan).

    The plan scopes by the walk's counted assets ("assets that don't exist
    yet"): instructions carry ``site_walk.site_walk_id`` and generation
    dispatches to site_walk_plan_service, which prices each walked service
    through its site_walk_config equation. Re-generating the plan re-reads
    the walk, so walk edits flow into the quote until it's accepted.

    Body: {site_walk_id: uuid, title?, opportunity_id?}.
    Returns the created + rendered plan (mirrors /plans/from-issues).

get.summary: Planned work orders across the company's ACCEPTED v2 quotes/EMPs — the
get.description:
Planned work orders across the company's ACCEPTED v2 quotes/EMPs — the
    pipeline that becomes real Work Orders on release. Released ones are
    excluded: they live on the Work Orders list now.

    RELEASE DETECTION IS THE DIRECT LINK, not signature matching. Releasing
    stamps ir_sessions.(plan_id, plan_workorder_id), so one query answers
    "which planned WOs are already out". The full execution walk
    (execution_status_for_plan) costs a per-plan session scan and exists to
    credit work that was NEVER released from the plan — irrelevant here, and it
    made this endpoint impossible to paginate.

    Query params (all optional):
      page, page_size, search, sort_by, sort_dir, sld_id, kind, bucket
      sort_by : window | label | plan_title | sld_name | kind | asset_count | est_mins
      bucket  : overdue | due_30 | due_quarter | due_year  (cumulative horizons)
    Response: {success, data: {items, total, page, page_size, total_pages, stats}}

get.summary: Cable library entries — aggregated across SKM cable rows.
get.description:
Cable library entries — aggregated across SKM cable rows.

    An "entry" is a logical cable spec the user picks from. The
    grouping key is ``(manufacturer, conductor_type, duct_material,
    installation, voltage, n_phase, n_num_conductors)``. **Conductor
    desc and insulation roll up** as multi-value attributes on the
    entry — same physical product is often offered in multiple
    conductor configurations (1/C, 3/C, 4/C, with/without ground)
    and insulation classes (THHN/XHHW/RHH/etc.). **Installation does
    NOT roll up** because per-size impedance specs in
    ``skm_cable_ac_sizes`` differ when the parent cable's installation
    differs (cable-in-conduit ≠ cable-in-air electrically).

    Each entry exposes:
      - ``conductor_descs[]``  — distinct conductor configs in the entry
      - ``insulation_classes[]`` — distinct insulation classes
      - ``sizes[]`` — union of sizes available across all variants
      - ``variants[]`` — full (cable_oid, conductor_desc,
        insulation_class, sizes[]) tuples for downstream binding

    Asset binding flow: user picks an entry → narrows
    conductor_desc + insulation_class → resolves to a specific
    ``cable_oid`` → picks a size → final binding is
    ``(cable_oid, size_id)``.

    Query params (all optional):
        conductor_type    str  exact match
        duct_material     str  exact match
        insulation_class  str  restrict to entries whose insulation
                                classes include this value
        insulation_type   str  exact match (str_insulation_type kept
                                ungrouped for now — granular)
        installation      str  exact match (entry-level)
        conductor_desc    str  restrict to entries whose conductor
                                descs include this value
        manufacturer      str  exact match
        voltage           num  exact match
        cable_size        str  restrict to entries that include this size
        limit             int  default 500, max 5000

get.summary: Everything needed to decide what a user may see, in one read.
get.description:
Everything needed to decide what a user may see, in one read.

      company_features   features the company is entitled to, each with the
                         permissions that gate it and whether this user holds one
      user_permissions   the caller's permissions, unioned across their roles
      user_roles         their active role assignments

    Roles are UNIONED, not pinned. A user sees an item if ANY of their roles
    grants it — 82 of 141 users hold more than one role, so pinning to a single
    role would hide pages they can genuinely reach. permission_service.
    get_user_roles() now applies the same rule, so what a user may SEE here and
    what a request may DO there are derived from one definition.

    A role assignment counts unless it is soft-deleted or expired. is_active is
    NOT tested: the app uses user_roles.is_active as a role SWITCHER, leaving
    one assignment on and the rest off, so testing it would report a four-role
    user as holding one role. Deletion and expiry are real revocations and are
    still honoured.

    Admin is NOT special-cased. Elsewhere an ADMIN_ROLES member short-circuits
    permission checks, but doing that here made the response self-contradictory:
    is_admin came from permission_service.is_admin(), which then collapsed to a
    single pinned role, while the permission union below did not — so a Client
    Portal + Admin user pinned to Client Portal was reported as not-admin while
    still holding Admin's grants. Every field now derives from the same union,
    and an admin appears here exactly as what their roles actually grant.

    Reports the CALLER only — there is no form for reading another user, so no
    admin check is needed and one user's roles can never leak to another.

    Read-only; touches no LaunchDarkly flag.

get.summary: Subscription banner for the caller's company
get.description:
Any signed-in user (T1 and T2). The company's current subscription is its active row, else its latest non-draft row (then `kind: expired`, and `term_end_at` is when it ended). `banner` is null when the company has no subscription (or can't be resolved), or there is nothing to announce — never a 400. The web app decides whether to show it (LaunchDarkly `subscription` flag); the API doesn't read LaunchDarkly.

Structured, not worded: the client builds the sentence and turns every `*_at` moment (ISO-8601 UTC) into a date and day count in the viewer's timezone, using `server_now` as "now". `kind` is one of `foundation_upcoming` | `foundation_full` | `foundation_grace` | `foundation_limited` | `renewal` | `expired`. A Foundation plan always has a banner (`dismissible: false`). `expiring` lists the term items (module, site or the subscription itself) ending inside the notice window, earliest first, with `renewal_cents` (null for legacy), plus the plan's `term_months` and `renewal_uplift_bps` for the renewal sentence — both price fields are null unless the caller is an admin. Foundation banners have `dismissible: false`; a dismissal is kept by the client per `dismiss_key`.

Display only: nothing is locked by the subscription.

get.summary: Subscription page for the caller's company
get.description:
Admin > Billing > Subscription. Admin, Super Admin and EG Admin only (403 otherwise). An expired plan (status expired / cancelled, or past its term end) is returned with `phase: expired`, `subscription.ended_at` and its last term; 404 only when the company has no non-draft subscription at all. Read only — subscriptions are edited in the database.

Items are read at one moment: now, clamped into the term (its start while `upcoming`, its last second once `expired`). Module and site plans run on their items, so `subscription.term_end_at` is the last item's end; `next_item_end_at` is the earliest live item's end.

All times are ISO-8601 UTC; all money is integer cents. `subscription.phase` is `upcoming` | `full` | `grace` | `limited` (Foundation) | `active` | `expiring` | `expired`. Each module's `access.code` is `included` | `until` | `shuts_down` | `locked` | `subscribed` | `sites` | `expired` | `starts` | `not_subscribed` | `coming_soon` | `separate_order` (`access.at` = the moment a dated label refers to; `sites_open` / `sites_total` for site plans). `sites` and `t2_licenses` carry each item's own term and `renewal_cents` (price × `policy.renewal_uplift_bps`). `fees.basis` is `contract` (foundation, legacy), `modules` or `sites`. Module / site plans: `annual_cents` = live items + the eg-ai tier (`ai_cents`), `renewal_cents` its next-term price, `module_count` / `site_count`; a module row's `counted` says whether it is in that total. Foundation: `list_cents` is the list price of the included modules + eg-ai, for reference. `ended` is true on an expired plan (the amounts are its last term). Legacy: `renewal_rate_card` is the current module rate card its renewal options come from. T2 is reported separately in `fees.t2_cents`, which is the T2 licences card's yearly total. `t2` is that card's first page of customer accounts (see GET /subscription/t2-accounts for the shape and paging). `usage.*.over` is true only when strictly above the plan limit. `activity` is derived from the company's subscription rows and their items, newest first, capped at the latest 100; `activity_total` is the full count.

404.description: `not_found` — the company can't be resolved, or has no subscription (none, or drafts only). Checked after the role.

403.description: `forbidden` — not an Admin, Super Admin or EG Admin.

get.summary: T2 licences card: the company's customer accounts, paged
get.description:
Admin, Super Admin and EG Admin only (403 otherwise). One row per customer account of the caller's company (ZP-4548): `tier` is the account's license type (`interactive` = Full Access, `read_only` = Lite, `no_license` = No License), `portal_users` its active portal seats, `annual_cents` the tier's price on the current rate card (No License 0; null when the card doesn't price the tier), and `term_start_at` / `term_end_at` the account's T2 licence on the subscription (null when there is none). Ordered Full Access, Lite, No License, then most portal users first. `counts` and `annual_cents` at the top level cover every account, not just the page.

Query: `page` (default 1), `page_size` (default 10, max 100).

403.description: `forbidden` — not an Admin, Super Admin or EG Admin.

get.summary: Serve the AASA file for iOS Universal Links.
get.description:
Serve the AASA file for iOS Universal Links.

    DEEP_LINK_IOS_APP_IDS takes a list, and every id in it is claimed for the
    same components. Listing every environment's app id is deliberate: for a
    wildcard entitlement Apple reads this file from the bare environment host
    (dev.egalvanic.ai), and those hosts are all answered by production, so a
    file naming only production's app would leave the dev and qa builds
    unverified. See DEEP_LINK_IOS_APP_IDS in config.py for the tradeoff.

    An environment with no iOS build claims no app IDs; the file is still served
    (with an empty ``details``) because 404 here would be rewritten to the SPA's
    index.html by CloudFront, which is harder to diagnose than an empty claim.

    **``webcredentials`` is a second, separate claim in the same file** (ZP-3896).
    ``applinks`` governs which URLs open in the app; ``webcredentials`` governs
    whether the app may use this host as a WebAuthn relying party and read
    shared-web-credential entries for it. iOS reads them independently, so a
    file with only ``applinks`` — which is what every tenant host served until
    now — leaves passkeys unusable on iOS even though deep links work:
    ``ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider`` fails as
    "unsupported" for a relying party the app is not associated with.

    The same app id list serves both. An app id is a claim about which builds
    this host trusts, and that answer does not differ between the two services.

    The host this file must be served from is the pool's ``RelyingPartyId``,
    which ZP-3920 made the tenant's own host (``<tenant>.<env>.egalvanic.ai``)
    rather than a shared apex — so it is this route, on the tenant host, and no
    apex DNS is involved. The app must also carry
    ``webcredentials:<that host>`` in its Associated Domains entitlement, which
    is the iOS half and not settable from here.

get.summary: Serve the Digital Asset Links file for Android App Links.
get.description:
Serve the Digital Asset Links file for Android App Links.

    DEEP_LINK_ANDROID_PACKAGE takes a list, and each package becomes its own
    statement — Android binds fingerprints to ONE package per statement, so
    claiming several means several statements, not one with several names.

    Listing every environment's package is deliberate here: for a wildcard
    entitlement the OS reads this file from the bare environment host
    (dev.egalvanic.ai), and those hosts are all answered by production, so a
    file naming only production's package would leave the dev and qa builds
    unverified. See DEEP_LINK_ANDROID_PACKAGE in config.py for what that
    tradeoff costs.

    Fingerprints are per package (see _fingerprints_for). A package with none
    configured is SKIPPED rather than published: a statement without a
    fingerprint is invalid, and an invalid statement can invalidate the file
    for every other package in it.

    **Each statement claims two relations** (ZP-3896): ``handle_all_urls`` for
    App Links, and ``get_login_creds`` for passkeys. Android's Credential
    Manager refuses to let an app act for a relying party without the second,
    so a file carrying only the first leaves passkeys unusable on Android while
    deep links work — the same split the iOS file has between ``applinks`` and
    ``webcredentials``, and the same failure if only one is present.

    The host this must be served from is the pool's ``RelyingPartyId``, which
    ZP-3920 made the tenant's own host, so it is this route on the tenant host.

    Rows are judged one by one: a row for an asset that is not a live asset of
    this site, or with a bad code, is listed in `failed` and the rest still

    a repeated save (double click, retry) changes nothing. A code another

    Returns:

        "success": true,
        "saved": [{"node_id": "uuid", "qr_code": "TS-001" | null}, ...],
        "unchanged": N,                                            // of `saved`
        "failed": [{"node_id": "uuid", "reason": "not_found" | "invalid" | "duplicate"}, ...]
    }

info.title: EG-PZ Backend API
info.description:
Comprehensive RESTful API for enterprise-grade electrical system management, infrared thermography analysis,
and preventive maintenance operations.

This API provides a complete suite of endpoints for managing electrical infrastructure data, thermal imaging sessions,
work orders, and comprehensive reporting capabilities. Built with security and scalability in mind, it supports
multi-tenant operations with AWS Cognito authentication.

**Key Capabilities:**
• Electrical system modeling with Single Line Diagrams (SLD)
• Infrared thermography session management and issue tracking
• Quote generation and work order planning
• Customer relationship management (Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities)
• Real-time push notifications for mobile devices
• Comprehensive reporting and analytics
• Dynamic form creation and data collection

**Technical Specifications:**
• RESTful architecture with JSON responses
• JWT-based authentication via AWS Cognito
• Rate limiting: 1000 requests/hour, 100 requests/minute
• Multi-tenant support with company-based data isolation
• Comprehensive data validation and error handling

**API Coverage:**
This documentation covers 190+ endpoints organized into 33 functional categories, providing complete
coverage for all system operations from authentication to reporting.

For technical support or API access, please contact: support@eg-pz.com

ChallengeV4Request.description:
Answer any Cognito challenge.

Superset of RespondToChallengeRequest: `code` carries a TOTP for
SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA / MFA_SETUP, `device_name` labels the authenticator in
Cognito's device list. Which fields are required depends on
challenge_name, so that check lives in the challenge registry
(app/services/cognito_challenge.py) rather than being duplicated per
challenge as separate schemas.
ChallengeV4Request.title: ChallengeV4Request

Set the MFA requirement for an organization or a single user.

One boolean, deliberately. The flags OR together
(app/services/mfa_policy.py), so there is no third "inherit" state to
express — and nothing here can relax a requirement that comes from the
pool's own MfaConfiguration.
MfaPolicyRequest.title: MfaPolicyRequest

TotpVerifyRequest.description: Confirm the first code from a freshly associated authenticator.
TotpVerifyRequest.title: TotpVerifyRequest

TotpRemoveRequest.description:
Turn off your own authenticator.

The code is step-up proof, not enrollment: Cognito has no "recently
authenticated" primitive, so possession of the factor being removed is the
only evidence available that the person holding this session is the person
who owns the account. Without it a stolen session strips the victim's second
factor permanently and silently, which is the one outcome that makes the
account materially easier to take over.
TotpRemoveRequest.title: TotpRemoveRequest

PasswordlessStartRequest.description:
Begin a passwordless sign-in — the passkey and email-code entry points.

Just an address and a tenant: the method is the endpoint, not a field, so a
caller cannot name a method the route did not gate. No password, and
deliberately nothing that would let the response differ between a registered
and an unregistered address.
PasswordlessStartRequest.title: PasswordlessStartRequest

PasskeyRegisterCompleteRequest.description: Finish registering a passkey. See ChallengeV4Request.credential.

PasskeyRemoveRequest.description:
Delete one of your own passkeys.

``credential_id`` is Cognito's own handle for the credential, taken from
GET /auth/v4/passkey/credentials and passed back untouched.

The pattern accepts BOTH base64 alphabets. A WebAuthn credential id is
base64-encoded binary, but which alphabet Cognito returns it in is not
documented and was not verified against a real credential — so pinning
base64url would have rejected a legitimate id outright the day
VALIDATION_MODE goes strict, for no gain. What it still rejects is the
thing worth rejecting: whitespace, quotes, control characters, anything
that is not an opaque token.

Bounded rather than free: a credential id is at most 1023 bytes raw, so no
encoding of one reaches 1400 characters.
PasskeyRemoveRequest.title: PasskeyRemoveRequest

GoogleCallbackQuery.description:

IrCreateAndExtractRequest.description:
Mobile FLIR camera app: create an ir_photo row and, for ``type='IR'``,
extract the embedded visual image from the FLIR radiometric JPEG in one call.

ZP-3112. ``type`` is the branch discriminator:
  - ``IR``     — FLIR capture; create row, then extract visual → S3.
  - ``VISUAL`` — plain visual capture; create row only, no extraction.

LEGACY body (the FLIR camera app): ``ir_session_id`` + ``ir_photo_key`` +
``visual_photo_key`` — the client chose the keys and uploaded under
``{ir_session_id}/{key}`` first; both keys are stored as sent.

CREATE-FIRST body (task #133): NO keys. The server mints the flat keys
(``ir-photos/{company}/{id}/…``), answers with presigned PUT URLs, and
extracts once the bytes are there (re-post the same ``id`` after the
PUT, or call the extraction routes). ``ir_session_id`` is then optional
(null = outside a work order); ``original_filename`` / ``ir_sha256`` /
``visual_file_name`` / ``service_id`` are the create-first fields
(app/services/ir_direct_upload.py).
IrCreateAndExtractRequest.title: IrCreateAndExtractRequest

IrDirectUploadPhoto.description:
One file pair of a direct upload (task #132). ``ir_sha256`` is the IR
file's SHA-256 (64 lower-case hex) — what a re-upload of the same file on
the same asset is deduped on. ``visual_file_name`` only when the client
has a separate visual file; without it the server extracts the embedded
visual after the upload (FLIR-IND-like). ``id`` is a client-minted row id
for offline replay.
IrDirectUploadPhoto.title: IrDirectUploadPhoto

IrDirectUploadRequest.description:
POST /node/<node_id>/ir-photos/direct: the IR photos a client is about
to upload on an asset OUTSIDE a work order. Bounds mirror
app/services/ir_direct_upload.py, which re-validates in every mode.
IrDirectUploadRequest.title: IrDirectUploadRequest

IrExtractVisualByFileNamesRequest.description:
Web bulk upload: names of the files just uploaded under <session_id>/.
The route matches them to the work order's IR photo rows and extracts the
FLIR-IND embedded visuals. Bounds mirror MAX_EXTRACT_FILE_NAMES in
ir_routes (enforced there too, since soft validation mode only logs).
IrExtractVisualByFileNamesRequest.title: IrExtractVisualByFileNamesRequest

IrRenderRequest.description: Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/render — edit params + output options.
IrRenderRequest.title: IrRenderRequest

IrStatsRequest.description: Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/stats — edit params only.
IrStatsRequest.title: IrStatsRequest

IrValueAtRequest.description: Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/value-at — thermal-space pixel + params.
IrValueAtRequest.title: IrValueAtRequest

IrProfileRequest.description: Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/profile — line orientation + index + params.
IrProfileRequest.title: IrProfileRequest

IrMeasureRequest.description:
Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/measure — a batch of measurement shapes
(spot/circle/rectangle/line) plus editor params. Shape geometry is validated
downstream by the IR microservice; kept permissive here.
IrMeasureRequest.title: IrMeasureRequest

IrSaveRequest.description:
Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/save — measurement set + editor params.

The microservice embeds the measurements as editable vectors in a radiometric
JPEG (replaces the IR object; stays editable + mobile-readable). ``image_base64``
is the client-baked visible image (shapes drawn) that becomes the visible JPEG
so SDK-less viewers see the shapes. An empty list clears all measurements.
IrSaveRequest.title: IrSaveRequest

IrRenameRequest.description:
Body for POST /ir_photo/<id>/rename — a new IR key and/or visual key.
The matching S3 object is moved and the DB row updated. At least one required
(enforced in the controller).
IrRenameRequest.title: IrRenameRequest

SldStreetViewRef.description:

A pano id, or the location (latitude + longitude), or both.

SldSetSitePhotoRequest.description:

user's own photo is saved with POST /photo/create, like other photos.)

Free-text ``*_name`` fields match case-insensitively (substring) on the
related name; ``*_id`` fields are exact UUID matches; ``procedure_count*``
filter the folded distinct-procedure count.

node_subtype_name.description: Substring match on asset subtype name
node_subtype_name.title: Node Subtype Name

pm_family_name.description: Substring match on PM family name

class. All fields optional; sensible defaults applied server-side.

search.title: Search

ShortcutByNodeClassV2Request.title: ShortcutByNodeClassV2Request

UltrasonicScanNodeCreateRequest.title: UltrasonicScanNodeCreateRequest

AddressVerificationBlock.description:
The ``address_verification`` block a site or account write may carry.

Its presence asks the server to re-check the address being saved; ``choice``
records which version the user picked after Verify. ``choice`` is recorded
only: the server never rewrites the address fields, so a client that picks
``normalized`` sends Google's version in those fields itself. ``token`` is
the ``verification_token`` /address/verify returned; for the same user and
address it stands in for a second Google call.
AddressVerificationBlock.title: AddressVerificationBlock

CreateAccountV2Contact.description: Primary contact created together with an account via POST /account/v2.
CreateAccountV2Contact.title: CreateAccountV2Contact

CreateAccountV2Request.description:
Single-call account + primary-contact creation.

Creates the account and the contact, links them (job_title lives on the
mapping), and flags the contact as the account default. Kept permissive so
the account-level address fields stay forgiving under the soft-validation
rollout; the nested `contact` object is strictly validated.
CreateAccountV2Request.title: CreateAccountV2Request

ListAccountsV2Filters.description:
Per-column free-text filters for the accounts v2 list.

Every field is optional free text; empty / missing means "no filter on
that column". `owner` matches the owning user's display name / username;
`company` matches the company name (both resolved via joins).
ListAccountsV2Filters.title: ListAccountsV2Filters

ListAccountsV2Request.description:
Server-side paginated / filtered account list.

Kept permissive (extra="allow") so the endpoint stays forgiving under the
soft-validation rollout; the handler still coerces/guards every field.
ListAccountsV2Request.title: ListAccountsV2Request

RouteStopAssetPayload.description:
One asset inside a stop, at its position in the worked order.

``position`` is 0-based and unique within the stop, but gaps are legal:
deleting an asset drops its row without resequencing the rest.
RouteStopAssetPayload.title: RouteStopAssetPayload

RouteStopPayload.description:
One room on the route.

``assets`` may be empty — a room qualifies as a stop through room activity,
not through assets.
RouteStopPayload.title: RouteStopPayload

RouteCreateRouteRequest.description:
A1 — ``POST /route/create``.

``id`` is required and client-generated: the device saved this route locally
and is already referencing it, so the server must store it under the id the
device knows.
RouteCreateRouteRequest.title: RouteCreateRouteRequest

RouteUpdateRouteRequest.description:
A2 — ``PUT /route/update/{route_id}``.

Every field is optional: this one endpoint carries a rename, a soft delete
and a full stop replacement, and a caller sends only what changed. When
``stops`` IS present it replaces the whole set — an omitted ``stops`` leaves
the existing ones alone, which is not the same as sending ``[]``.
RouteUpdateRouteRequest.title: RouteUpdateRouteRequest

RouteRunAssetPayload.description: A manual "processed" mark on one of the run's stop assets.
RouteRunAssetPayload.title: RouteRunAssetPayload

RouteRunStopPayload.description:
A COMPLETED stop of a run.

``completed_by`` NULL means the completion materialized automatically once
every effective stop asset was worked; a user id means someone marked the
visit complete by hand.
RouteRunStopPayload.title: RouteRunStopPayload

RouteRunUpdateRunRequest.description:
R2 — ``PUT /route_run/update/{run_id}``.

``stops`` and ``assets`` are full replacement and may SHRINK: unmarking a
visit removes a completion row. Any status is accepted, including the two
reopening transitions (``FINISHED -> ACTIVE`` when a visit is unmarked,
``ABANDONED -> ACTIVE`` when a paused run is resumed).
RouteRunUpdateRunRequest.title: RouteRunUpdateRunRequest

SiteWalkIssueUpdateRequest.description:
A reviewer's edit to an interpreter-proposed walk issue. Every field
optional: only what is sent changes. `details` REPLACES the whole array —
send it only to set every answer (on a class change, omit it and the
server carries over the answers whose names the classes share).

Documentation, not the gate: VALIDATION_MODE defaults to soft, and
site_walk_issue_service.update_issue re-checks everything that matters.
SiteWalkIssueUpdateRequest.title: SiteWalkIssueUpdateRequest

read from request.files and format-sniffed from its bytes in the
controller); these are the text fields that accompany it.
